title: Air-gapped dual-NIC BMC bootstrap — terraform sketch & upgrade plan
body:
Context / goal:
- Goal: a repeatable on-prem cluster bootstrap for air-gapped customer sites that use a dedicated management NIC (BMC/IPMI) and a separate data NIC (tenant network). The playbook focuses on minimal trust surface for the air-gap, fast reprovisioning via BMC + iPXE, and Terraform-driven provisioning of baremetal inventory + vSphere VM templates.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Two-phase approach: 1) Provision management plane (BMC, DHCP/TFTP/IPXE, local package mirror) 2) Bootstrap control plane + workers via kubeadm with local image registry and offline CRI images.
- Use Terraform to maintain inventory and generate per-host iPXE boot configs; use small modules: bm_inventory, ipxe_server, mirror_registry, vsphere_vm_provision.
- Upgrade strategy: canary 1 control-plane node -> remaining control-plane -> workers, with automated smoke tests and rollback images preserved.

Design constraints / assumptions:
- Customer environment is fully air-gapped: no outbound internet. Packages and images are delivered on a USB or internal mirror appliance.
- Each physical host has at least two NICs: mgmt (BMC + isolated DHCP/iPXE) and data (pod/node traffic).
- BMC reachable from ops network VM only; BMC credentials are stored in customer vault (we store pointers in Terraform state, not secrets in repo).

Important links / refs:
- terraform-modules: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules (module names below reference that repo)
- JIRA-PRIVDEP-412 (umbrella for air-gap work)
- confluence:Onprem-Bootstrap-Playbook (long-form runbook)

High-level steps (playbook):
1) Prep and inventory
   - Collect BMC IPs, vendor type (ipmi/idrac/iLO), firmware versions.
   - Capture MACs for both NICs and expected device naming on OS (we prefer predictable NIC mapping via udev tags).
   - Prepare USB bundle: OS images (netboot kernel/initrd), containerd/crictl, kubeadm binaries, kubelet, offline tarball of control-plane images, registry mirror archive.

2) Infra: IPXE + DHCP + mirror
   - Stand up an isolated management VM running: dnsmasq (DHCP/TFTP), iPXE HTTP server, and a simple registry mirror (Harbor/registry:2 with preloaded blobs).
   - Terraform module: ipxe_server creates a VM and uploads iPXE templates; bm_inventory registers hosts and renders per-host iPXE configs.
   - Verify iPXE can chainload kernel+initrd from USB or internal HTTP.

3) Provision OS via iPXE + BMC power cycle
   - Use Terraform (bm_provision) to call ipmitool/Redfish actions against BMC to set next-boot to PXE and power-cycle.
   - Kick off kickstart/cloud-init with the OS image that includes our pre-baked packages (kubeadm, containerd) or run minimal bootstrap scripts to fetch packages from the mirror.
   - Post-install: ensure both NICs present and named; tag mgmt interface in /etc/network/interfaces.

4) Bootstrap control plane (offline kubeadm)
   - On first control-plane node (canary): load container images into containerd: ctr images import path/to/offline-images.tar.gz
   - kubeadm init --config /etc/kubernetes/kubeadm-config.yaml --ignore-preflight-errors=SystemVerification
   - Install local registry mirror and set imagePullSecrets/policy to point to mirror.
   - Apply network plugin: we recommend Calico with manifest rewritten to use image from mirror.

5) Join remaining control planes and workers
   - Use kubeadm join tokens generated during init (we persist tokens as short-lived artifacts in the local mirror VM for bootstrapping).
   - Validate etcd cluster health after each control-plane join: kubectl get componentstatuses; ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl endpoint status

6) Post-bootstrap validations
   - Node readiness, pod network connectivity, DNS resolution, image pull from local mirror, CRI runtime logs.
   - Run small inference smoke test harness (local binary) to ensure model-serving containers can start (this prevents subtle regression like wrong seccomp profile causing image OOM).

Terraform module notes (sketch):
- Module: bm_inventory (inputs/outputs)
  - variables: list(map) hosts = [{name, bmc_ip, mgmt_mac, data_mac, vendor, location}]
  - outputs: host_objects (rendered metadata), ipxe_entries (per-host URL)
  - behavior: renders iPXE templates (using template_file) and uploads them to ipxe_server via remote-exec or API.

- Module: ipxe_server
  - variables: vm_image, ssh_key, mirror_artifacts (list of files to seed), dhcp_range, tftp_root
  - outputs: ipxe_base_url, mirror_registry_url
  - notes: intentionally minimal; prefer idempotent scripts for template upload.

- Module: mirror_registry
  - variables: images_tarball_path, storage_size_gb
  - outputs: registry_endpoint, credentials_secret_id
  - behavior: creates VM with mounted volume, starts registry:2 and preloads images via registry importer.

- Module: vsphere_vm_provision (for customers using vSphere)
  - variables: template_name, cpu, memory, network_map, datastore, extra_config
  - outputs: vm_id, guest_ip
  - note: cloud-init injection is tricky in air-gap; we bake cloud-init userdata into template and then use guest customization to set hostnames only.

Implementation notes and pitfalls we've hit in prior runs (from experiments):
- BMC rate-limiting: some vendors will throttle repeated IPMI calls; implement backoff in terraform external provisioner or use a tiny control-plane to queue BMC actions.
- iPXE + initramfs mismatch: ensure kernel and initramfs pair match exact OS minor version. In air-gap we saw kernel module load failures when mismatched.
- /dev/disk/by-* naming changes: enforce persistent naming by writing udev rules referencing mac addresses.
- vSphere tools: OVF property injection can be flaky on older vCenters; prefer templated OVA per site when possible.

Upgrade plan (k8s + runtime + OS) — draft:
- Principles:
  - Keep cluster API reachable during upgrade; avoid upgrading >1 control plane simultaneously unless running >3 control planes with quorum preserved.
  - Always preserve old images in the mirror for rollback.
  - Automate smoke tests that validate core API, scheduling, and model-serving probe.

- Canary upgrade flow (control plane):
  1) Prepare mirror with kubeadm/binaries for target version (X.Y.Z) and all CRI images.
  2) Drain canary control-plane? (control planes shouldn't be drained for static workloads) — we patch kubeadm config on node and run kubeadm upgrade apply --config new-config on the canary node.
  3) Wait for etcd snapshot success and health checks. Run smoke tests.
  4) If OK, sequentially upgrade other control-plane nodes (one at a time).

- Worker upgrade flow:
  1) Cordon and drain worker nodes (graceful eviction with timeouts tuned for model containers).
  2) Reprovision runtime (containerd) from mirror if runtime format changes.
  3) kubeadm upgrade node/config --kubelet-version ... and restart kubelet.
  4) Uncordon and run workload-specific readiness checks.

Rollback plan (fast):
- If canary fails, stop the rollout and:
  - Restore etcd snapshot taken immediately before canary upgrade.
  - Re-register failed node in previous image (we keep previous containerd/kubelet binaries staged on the mirror with tags like vX.Y.Z-rollback).
  - Revert kubeadm config on upgraded control plane nodes via kubeadm downgrade steps (documented per version).

Testing / verification checklist (pre-upgrade):
- Automated smoke tests passing against mirror cluster (control-plane + sample model server).
- Etcd backup exists and is verified (test restore in a lab).
- All images for new version present in mirror and pre-pulled on at least one node.
- BMC access validated for every host (power cycle test).

Operational runbook fragments (for on-call):
- If node never becomes Ready after join: check containerd import logs (ctr images ls), check CRI socket path, inspect kernel modules (missing overlayfs?).
- If pods stuck ImagePullBackOff: confirm registry TLS cert and CA on node. Air-gap sites often require that we install customer root CA into system store before docker/containerd TLS handshake.
- If etcd quorum lost: take snapshot from most recent healthy node, bring up new control plane with --experimental-control-plane-creation? (documented steps in confluence).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether to support k0s/k3s as a lightweight alternative for 1-2 node remote sites (pros: single binary; cons: drift from kubeadm flows we already support).
- We need an operator to manage mirror lifecycle (garbage collection of old images) and a signed manifest format for images to guarantee integrity in air-gap.
- Improve terraform BMC provider: current approach uses local-exec ipmitool wrappers; evaluate a small Go-based controller to serialize BMC actions and surface richer errors.

Notes to self / action items:
- (Aisha) prototype template renderer for iPXE snippets and put into terraform-modules repo as bm_inventory module.
- (Luca) test BMC backoff strategies with Dell iDRAC and Supermicro IPMI; capture vendor-specific quirks.
- (Maya) build a smoke-test harness that runs inside the mirror VM and can be invoked by CI when building the mirror artifact.

Appendix: example kubeadm-config (minimal, show values to be templated)
- kubeadm config YAML (short):
  apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta3
  kind: ClusterConfiguration
  kubernetesVersion: vX.Y.Z
  controlPlaneEndpoint: "lb.mgmt.local:6443"
  imageRepository: "mirror.local:5000/k8s"

- Example ipmi power-cycle (used by terraform external script):
  ipmitool -I lanplus -H ${BMC_IP} -U ${BMC_USER} -P ${BMC_PASS} chassis bootdev pxe
  ipmitool -I lanplus -H ${BMC_IP} -U ${BMC_USER} -P ${BMC_PASS} power cycle

Last notes: keep this doc intentionally sketchy — it's a middle layer between the long-form runbook and the terraform modules. Expect edits after initial proving at customer site.

Unresolved: exact naming of terraform state secrets (vault vs sops) — prefer vault references in state, but need ops runbook for emergency manual actions.

Chatter / meeting log snippets:
- 2025-12-12: discussed adding cfssl-based CA rotation to mirror VM so we can issue node certs for TLS without customer involvement. Action: spike (Noah).
- 2026-01-20: vendor feedback: some older iLOs do not accept Redfish power commands reliably; keep ipmitool fallback.

End of draft.
